title: Minimum Cost to Connect Two Groups of Points
summary: Given two groups of points with sizes size1 and size2 (where size1 is greater than or equal to size2), a cost matrix of size1 x size2 defines the connection costs between points in the two groups.
statement: Given two groups of points with sizes size1 and size2 (where size1 is greater than or equal to size2), a cost matrix of size1 x size2 defines the connection costs between points in the two groups. The task is to find the minimum cost to connect each point in the first group to at least one point in the second group, and each point in the second group to at least one point in the first group.
constraints: cost is a 1-through-12 by 1-through-12 positive matrix.
Choose connections so every vertex in both groups has at least one incident connection.
Return the minimum sum of selected connection costs.
hints: Track which right-group vertices are covered after processing each left vertex.
Connect each left vertex once in the main DP, then cheaply attach any still-uncovered right vertices.
Transition mask to mask|1<<column; afterward add each missing column’s cheapest incident edge.
An optimum can designate one selected edge per left vertex; any additional selected edge is needed only to cover a missing right vertex and can be replaced by its cheapest incident edge.
editorial: An optimum can designate one selected edge per left vertex; any additional selected edge is needed only to cover a missing right vertex and can be replaced by its cheapest incident edge.

tests.explanation: Connect the first left point to the first right point for fifteen and the second pair for two, totaling seventeen.
The first row connects to column zero, and the second row can cover columns one and two for a total of three.
